propositions: A patch-set upload event is delivered at-most-once by Gerrit webhook and then permanently dropped by the reconciler when the cursor advances to newest event time without a low-water mark for failed candidates

The reconciler's cursor persists unconditionally to the max event time in a fetch window, excluding retryably-abandoned candidates from all future windows even though the reconciler is contracted to re-drive them
A change stalls unvoted indefinitely until a human manually posts recheck-review or rebases, both of which mint a new events-log event with timestamp after the cursor to re-admit the change

The guarding test suite contains a false green: the fake events-log records the since parameter but ignores it, never exercising the production cursor filter on multi-event windows with mid-window failures
Three observable states (bot down, review running, queued-behind-N, dropped-permanently) are indistinguishable today, preventing correct triage when a change stalls
